description: GitHub issue triage (jev-triage's job): issue kind plus whether it includes reproduction steps.

kind.instructions: What kind of GitHub issue is this?

criteria.bug: Something that should work does not: errors, crashes, wrong output, regressions.
criteria.feature: A request for new behavior, options, or an improvement to existing behavior.
criteria.question: Asking how to do something or whether something is possible; nothing is claimed broken.
criteria.docs: Documentation is missing, wrong, unclear, or has typos.

has_repro.instructions: Does the issue include a command, a code snippet, or numbered steps that someone else could follow to reproduce what it describes? Pointing at a location in the docs or describing the symptom does not count.

criteria.true: Has concrete reproduction steps, snippet, or commands

state.title: Jobs occasionally run twice after upgrading to 5.4
state.body: We run the scheduler on three worker nodes behind a load balancer and since upgrading from 5.3 to 5.4 last week some jobs run twice. It does not happen every day. On Monday our nightly invoice job ran twice and sent duplicate invoices to about forty customers, which was embarrassing, and on Thursday the cleanup job ran twice, which is harmless but shows the same thing. Both times the two runs started within a second of each other on different nodes. Before the upgrade we never saw this in two years of use. We have not changed our configuration, the database is the same Postgres 15 instance, and the clocks on the nodes are synced with NTP. The logs on both nodes say they acquired the job lock, which should not be possible. We have rolled back to 5.3 for now, but we would like to upgrade eventually because of the memory fixes in 5.4. Happy to share more logs if someone can tell us what to look for.

cases.rationale: A regression that should not happen is a bug; the long description gives no commands, code or steps.

state.title: Sharing the cache between parallel CI jobs?
state.body: We are moving our monorepo from Jenkins to GitHub Actions and the build currently takes about twenty minutes, most of which is the tool re-analysing files that have not changed. On Jenkins we had a single long-lived machine, so the local cache directory just stayed warm between builds. On Actions every job starts on a fresh runner, and we run about six jobs in parallel for different packages. I have read the caching section of the docs, which explains the cache directory and the cache key, but it only talks about a single machine. Is it possible to share one cache between parallel jobs, for example by restoring it with actions/cache at the start of each job? If so, is it safe for several jobs to write to it at the same time, or should each package have its own cache key? And would a cache made on Linux runners be usable on our macOS runners, or does it contain anything platform-specific? Any pointers from people who have set this up would be appreciated.

cases.rationale: Asks whether and how something is possible, claims nothing is broken: question.
